short: Below the seam: runtime, port, programs, forms
is: Everything below the seam: one ManagedRuntime, one `ZurfurApi` port, outcome-returning programs per domain, one Schema module per form.
conventions: Programs return an OUTCOME UNION (data or a renderable Problem), not a raw Effect — loads/actions `runApi(program)` and branch.
Ports by role with a prod Layer and an in-memory test Layer (`zurfurApiTest`) — adapter-mem parity; specs never touch the network.
Validation is server-side; browser `required` is a courtesy.
Auth-time accepts what claim-time rejects: punycode handles pass `handleField` at sign-in, fail `claimHandleField` at account creation.

fs.name: *.spec.ts
fs.role: node-project specs beside each program module (accounts, session, den, api-proxy, session-headers, session-gate, frame-headers, handle-chain, error-log); den/den-path.spec.ts holds the path-handling security cases

fs.name: accounts.ts
fs.role: account programs (accountsOutcome, accountOutcome, create/deleteAccountOutcome); the delete's API path goes through path-builder.ts

fs.name: api-proxy.ts
fs.role: pure rewriteApiRequest + extractSessionCookie used by hooks.server.ts and session-headers.ts (no $env, unit-tests standalone)

fs.name: api/
fs.role: the backend port + tagged error union + generated protobuf messages

fs.name: den-served.ts
fs.role: denServed(): whether this run can show a Den — the mock only, for now; fails closed (false) on the everyday stack, so the frame shows no sidebar, tree or My Den links there

fs.name: den.ts
fs.role: the den page's program: read the node at an address through the port (and, on a full page load, its ancestors' listings in parallel), map the read to the web's Den view with every link built by the path builder; outcomes: page / reload (stale token) / signedOut

fs.name: den/
fs.role: den-path.ts — the Den path builder: browser pathname → segments (decoded once, allowlisted, ≤16), allowlisted query (includeDeleted, pageToken), the only DenHref mint, the API path

fs.name: error-log.ts
fs.role: pure logUnexpectedError (hooks.server.ts's handleError): logs route template + status only, returns a fixed message

fs.name: forms/
fs.role: one Effect Schema per form (login, create-account, delete-account) over a shared handle field; problem-message.ts bridges a Problem onto the superform message

fs.name: frame-headers.ts
fs.role: refuseFraming handle hook: Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none' and X-Frame-Options: DENY on every response

fs.name: handle-chain.ts
fs.role: handleChain(...handles): the handle hooks as one, first outermost — a plain stand-in for SvelteKit's sequence, which needs the live request store and can't be unit-tested

fs.name: path-builder.ts
fs.role: the one way a path is put together from pieces: each piece a minted PathSegment, `%` escaped, then parsed back to prove the URL parser reads exactly what was built; used by the Den path builder and the account-delete call

fs.name: runtime.ts
fs.role: THE SEAM — process-wide ManagedRuntime; runApi is the only Effect→Promise crossing

fs.name: session-gate.ts
fs.role: the sign-in gate, the one real one: a handle hook that, for every (session) route (page, __data.json whatever it skips, form action), asks the backend who is signed in and redirects to /login if nobody is, before any load or action runs; hands the session to the root layout through locals. The sign-out action is let through, so it can always clear the browser's session

fs.name: session-headers.ts
fs.role: pure sessionHeaders handle hook used by hooks.server.ts: marks every response to a request carrying the session cookie Cache-Control: private, no-store and Referrer-Policy: same-origin
